## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503 Incident

**Prepared:** 2026-08-26 · from `logs/gateway.log`, `logs/worker.log`, `deploys.csv`
**Status at end of available data: UNRESOLVED — still failing when the log capture ends.**

> **Read this first:** the log entries are dated **2026-03-14**, not last night. Either this capture is from an older incident or the files are stale. Confirm which before acting on the rollback.

---

### TL;DR

Roll back **dep-4471** (gateway config, a.novak). It flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true`, which exhausted a fixed 20-connection pool within seconds. 530 requests returned 503 — 83% of user traffic — and it was still going 1h45m later.

---

### Root cause

At `02:13:41.234Z` the gateway applied config generation 119:

```
gateway.pool.perRequest:     false -> true     <-- this one
gateway.timeout.upstreamMs:  2000  -> 2500
gateway.log.sampleRate:      1.0   -> 1.0      (no-op)
```

With `perRequest=true`, each in-flight request holds its own pool connection instead of multiplexing. The pool is fixed at 20. It saturated immediately and never recovered: `in_use=20 idle=0` in every `pool stats` line from 02:15 onward, with the wait queue climbing from 13 to 271.

Every failed request carries the same error, and it is the **only** error code in the file:

```
ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

**All 530 503s pair 1:1 with an `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` on the same request id** — zero unmatched in either direction.

Corroborating signal at `03:02:30Z`: `connection churn: 4180 opens in the last 5m, baseline is 40` — ~104× normal, exactly what per-request connections produce.

**The upstreams were never the problem.** Successful requests show unchanged latency across the boundary (~101ms avg before, ~103ms after) and `pool_wait` never exceeded 3ms on any 200. Failures hit all four upstreams evenly (132–133 each) and all five `/v1/` routes evenly (106 each) — a gateway-local fault, not a sick dependency. The 503s land at 600–999ms, well under the 2500ms upstream timeout, so it's the pool acquire timing out.

---

### Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **Last clean request** | `02:13:41.234Z` (req-07307, 200) |
| **Config applied** | `02:13:41.234Z` |
| **First 503** | `02:14:18.972Z` — req-07401 `/v1/cart -> billing-svc` |
| **Time from config to first failure** | **37 seconds** |
| **On-call paged** | `03:21:05.282Z` — 67 min after first 503 |
| **Last data point** | `03:59:27.974Z` — still 503, error rate still 83% |
| **Observed duration** | **≥ 1h 45m, no recovery in the log** |

Error rate by 10-min bucket: `0%` through 02:10 → **44%** (02:10 bucket, partial) → **83% flat** from 02:20 through the end. 530 × 503 vs 698 × 200.

Affected: `/v1/cart`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/session` — including checkout, so this is revenue-impacting.

**`/health` returned zero 503s.** It doesn't acquire a pool connection, so it stayed green the entire time while 83% of real traffic failed. That is almost certainly why the load balancer never pulled the node — and it's the single most important follow-up here.

---

### Roll back: dep-4471

```
dep-4471 | gateway | 2026-03-14 02:12→02:14Z | a.novak
         | "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"
```

Timeline is unambiguous — 12s from deploy start to the reload appearing in the log, 37s from config applied to first 503.

**Rollback = revert config generation 119 → 118**, or at minimum set `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`. The `upstreamMs` 2000→2500 change is inert here (nothing got far enough to hit an upstream timeout) but revert it with the generation for cleanliness.

**Ruled out — do not roll these back:**

- **dep-4472** (billing-svc, 02:41) and **dep-4473** (catalog-svc, 03:20) — both shipped *after* the error rate was already at 83%, and neither changed the error rate or the distribution across upstreams.
- **dep-4470** (worker, 00:48–00:55) — gateway ran clean for 79 minutes after it finished: 632 consecutive 200s, `waiting=0` throughout.

---

### Before you close it out

1. **Check whether nodes 1 and 2 got generation 119.** This log is `node-3 of 3` and I only have node-3's data. If the config rolled fleet-wide, all three are affected and the rollback must cover all three.
2. **Confirm the current live value of `gateway.pool.perRequest`.** There is **no rollback recorded in `deploys.csv`** — the revert either happened after these files were captured, or it never happened.
3. **Fix the health check.** `/health` not touching the pool made this incident invisible to the LB for 67 minutes. Either route it through a pool acquire or add a separate readiness probe that does.
4. **Fix alerting.** 67 minutes from first 503 to page, on an 83% error rate. The page fired on a 5-minute average crossing 71%; something should fire far earlier than that.
5. The stated intent was "pool isolation" — if that goal still stands, it needs a pool-size increase sized to peak concurrency shipped *together with* the `perRequest` flip, not the flip alone.

---

### Separate issue — not part of this incident, but don't lose it

`worker.log` shows **zero errors** across all 1,080 jobs (all `finished ok`), and the worker pool never moved off `size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0`. The workers did not hit the gateway trouble.

But job durations grow linearly all window, **200ms → 2,324ms (11×)**, at a steady ~+11ms/min with **no inflection at 02:13:41** — it was already 5× underway before the gateway config changed. `db_wait` stays flat at 0–12ms, so it's not the database. The ramp is already in progress at the first log line, so it started before 01:00; **dep-4470** ("retry backoff for webhook jobs", finishing 00:55Z) is the only candidate in the CSV but I can't confirm it without worker logs from before 01:00.

**Why it matters:** every job still returns `ok`, so no alert will ever fire. At the observed slope it crosses 3s around 04:30 and keeps climbing. Worth its own ticket.

Also open and pre-existing: `WARN db slow query 1.9s: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = ? — unindexed scan, known issue OPS-2210` (one occurrence, 02:36:22Z, did not cause contention).

---

*Data caveat: both logs contain non-monotonic timestamps (86 of 2,013 lines in `gateway.log`; also present in `worker.log`). All figures above key off parsed timestamps rather than line order, so they're unaffected — but don't trust strict line ordering if you script against these files. The `waiting` counter in `gateway.log`'s periodic `pool stats` lines also wraps back to 12 at 03:15:58; that's a counter artifact, not a recovery — `in_use=20 idle=0` never changes.*

Want me to save this to a file in the working directory?
